basic_info.name: MiiHealth AI - DAINA (Dynamic AI Intake and Navigation Agent)
basic_info.description: MiiHealth AI is a Phoenix, Arizona digital-health startup whose product, DAINA (Dynamic AI Intake and Navigation Agent), is an autonomous, multilingual voice agent that calls or greets a patient before an appointment, conducts a natural multi-turn clinical intake interview in the patient's preferred language using specialty-specific protocols, detects red flags, and writes a structured, clinician-ready intake note (HPI plus history, goals and medication adherence) directly into the EHR. It is deliberately positioned as the pre-visit counterpart to ambient scribes: it runs before the clinician is in the room rather than transcribing a conversation that already happened. The single most load-bearing fact for MediKiosk is that a funded, Mayo-Clinic-validated company has now proven the exact commercial thesis Module C depends on - that patient-elicited pre-visit history can be turned into a structured note that saves clinician time (company-reported ~8 minutes saved per encounter, ~2 hours/provider/day, 93% patient 'easy to use') - while doing so entirely cloud-first, US-market, English/Spanish-centric, and against EHR-native fields rather than an open national FHIR document contract like NRCeS OPConsultRecord.
basic_info.organization: MiiHealth AI (MiiHealth Corporation), Phoenix, Arizona; founded/relocated from London 2024. Leadership: Kelvin Summoogum (CEO, previously MiiCare, a 2024 Mayo Clinic & ASU MedTech Accelerator alumnus), John Wall (CPO), Debayan 'Dexter' Das (Chief AI Officer, built Mediiflow), Josh Becker (COO), Marcela Summoogum (Chief Clinical Officer).
basic_info.country: United States (operations previously London, UK; primary market US, with a stated focus on older adults and specialty clinics)
basic_info.status: pilot (seed-funded commercial startup moving from clinical validation to deployment; Mayo Clinic know-how collaboration and pilot completed, no confirmed broad production rollout)

technical_features.what_it_does: Conducts autonomous pre-visit patient intake. DAINA calls the patient before the appointment (or greets them on a tablet/kiosk in the exam room or clinic), sets expectations, and holds a multi-turn natural-language clinical interview in the patient's preferred language. Using specialty-specific protocols it captures symptoms and current presentation, medical/clinical history, visit goals, medication adherence, and red-flag symptoms, prioritising the most critical questions first so staff can be alerted when needed. It then generates a concise, structured, specialty-specific HPI/intake note with red flags and triage categories that a provider reviews and edits into the EHR before the encounter. It explicitly does not diagnose; red flags are surfaced for a human. The company claims the engine returns >2 hours/day per provider and ~8 minutes saved per visit.
technical_features.architecture: Proprietary agentic voice AI stack wrapped in a product called 'Mediiflow', described as 'the world's first clinic-ready AI intake engine'. Mediiflow ingests unstructured organisational know-how (doctor notes, hospital guidelines, SOPs) into a structured knowledge graph, transforms it into repeatable 'protocols' that DAINA executes, and captures/syncs structured outputs. DAINA is described as an 'embodied conversational AI agent' running across phone, web, mobile, tablet, and provider-PC channels. The exact foundation models, ASR/TTS vendors, orchestration framework, and reasoning/safety-check implementation are NOT publicly disclosed [uncertain]. Integration is stated as HL7v2 plus 'other standards'. The model/pipeline is not described as on-device.
technical_features.inputs: Patient voice during a phone call or in-person tablet/kiosk session; specialty-specific protocols; organisation-supplied documents/guidelines/SOPs used to build those protocols; and (per the Mayo pilot) patient-reported symptoms, history, medication adherence and goals. No document/paper-scan digitisation pipeline is described, and no structured FHIR input is described.
technical_features.outputs: Structured, EHR-ready intake notes: a concise HPI/pre-visit summary highlighting key symptoms, clinical history and red flags; intake forms; red-flag alerts; triage categories; and structured data mapped to the appropriate clinical fields (with 'Copy to EHR'). Delivery is into the EHR via HL7v2 and 'other standards'. Outputs are NOT described as an interoperable FHIR Composition/Bundle or a national-IG-conformant document.
technical_features.standards_compliance: Claimed/used: HL7v2 for EHR integration plus unspecified 'other integration standards'; HIPAA-oriented posture and BAA framing; dedicated Microsoft Azure single-tenant hosting with region choice (US-East, US-West, Azure Gov). No evidence of FHIR, HL7 IPS, SNOMED CT, LOINC, ICD, or any national FHIR Implementation Guide (NRCeS/ABDM OPConsultRecord, HealthDocumentRecord, INPS) conformance or validation. The company is US-market and describes no Indian standards. Conformance claims are vendor-stated and not independently validated [uncertain].
technical_features.offline_capability: None documented. Architecture is cloud-based (dedicated per-tenant Microsoft Azure hosting explicitly sold as a data-sovereignty feature). No on-device inference, local storage, store-and-forward sync, or offline mode is described. The chosen data-sovereignty options are US regions plus Azure Gov, i.e. US-only residency.
technical_features.languages_supported: Marketed as multilingual - 'intake patients in any language at scale', engaging in the patient's preferred language and in 'culturally sensitive dialogue'; examples cite English and Spanish. No Devanagari/Hindi or code-mixed Hinglish support is documented, and the exact supported language list and language-quality evidence are not published [uncertain].
technical_features.deployment_model: Cloud SaaS in a dedicated, isolated single-tenant Microsoft Azure environment per hospital/department, with guaranteed CPU/GPU quotas and a choice of US-East, US-West or Azure Gov (future geo-expansion stated but not delivered). Patient-facing channels: outbound phone call, and in-person tablet/kiosk/PC; the Specialities page markets 'in-clinic (tablet/kiosk) or pre-visit (phone)'. No local server or on-device requirement is published. Hardware is limited to the patient endpoint (phone or tablet/kiosk).

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: No published accuracy/F1/ROUGE/BERTScore/concept-recall figures, and no publicly reported error rate, omission rate, or note-fidelity benchmark. The reported figures are operational and experiential, and are vendor/company-reported (Mayo Clinic Arizona outpatient arrhythmia clinic pilot, Jul-Sep 2025): 97.9% intake completion (235/240 patients); patient survey - 93% found it easy to use (216/233), 91% easy to understand (213/233), 82% comfortable sharing information (191/233), 82% would use it again (150/230), 79% said the visit had more decision time (113/143); treating cardiology clinicians (n=4) reported no safety concerns; estimated time saved 1-10 min/visit with average AI interaction time ~8 minutes. Commercial claims (not a controlled study): ~8 minutes saved per patient visit, 93% of patients find it easy to use, and ~$3,600 saved monthly per $90/hour provider (16 patients/provider/day -> >2 hours/day). A later statement reports 300+ patients across two cardiology workflows. NONE of these are independent, peer-reviewed, or audited; clinical-accuracy and safety metrics are absent [uncertain].
performance_metrics.latency: No explicit latency or time-to-note figure is published. The closest datapoint is an average AI interaction time of ~8 minutes per intake in the Mayo Clinic pilot, which is a conversation duration, not a system latency [uncertain].
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: No published RAM/CPU/GPU/model-size requirements for a customer. The vendor runs inference in its own dedicated Azure tenancy with reserved CPU/GPU quotas, so the customer endpoint only needs a phone or a tablet/kiosk browser. No on-premise or edge footprint is offered [uncertain].
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: 300+ patients across two cardiology intake workflows in work with Mayo Clinic (company-reported); a Mayo Clinic Arizona arrhythmia-clinic pilot of 240 patients (Jul-Sep 2025) with 235 completions; 200+ patients cited at the earlier collaboration announcement. Company size/headcount and total customer count are not disclosed. Funding: $2.8M seed (August 2026).
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: A company-run pilot with Mayo Clinic (Arizona, outpatient arrhythmia clinic, Jul-Sep 2025): 240 patients invited to DAINA intake, 235 completed; a post-intake patient survey (denominators 233/230/143) and informal clinician feedback from 4 cardiologists reporting no safety concerns; estimated time-saved range 1-10 min/visit. There was no public protocol, no randomised control, no independent adjudication, no blinded note-quality review, and no peer-reviewed publication of record. The later business-press figures (8 min/visit, 93% ease, $3,600/month, 300+ patients) are company-reported marketing claims; the pilot-survey numbers are company-reported via LinkedIn. Independent third-party market analysis (DevCuration, distilinfo) explicitly cautions that these are not independently audited and that accuracy/false-omission/false-flag behaviour is unproven [uncertain]. The clinical-accuracy dimension is the single biggest evidence gap: a pre-visit intake agent's most important safety metric is whether its structured note faithfully and completely represents what the patient said without fabricating or omitting, and no such metric has been published.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: DAINA is the closest funded, clinically-piloted prior art to MediKiosk Module C, and it matters in three ways. (1) It validates the market thesis end-to-end at the precise layer MediKiosk operates in - a patient-elicited pre-visit history can be converted into a structured, provider-ready note that returns measurable clinician time and is accepted by patients and cardiologists at a top-tier institution (Mayo Clinic). This is stronger evidence than an ambient scribe because it proves the pre-visit, patient-elicited workflow the MediKiosk problem statement asks for. (2) It demonstrates the product shape Module C should imitate: specialty-specific protocol-driven elicitation, red-flag prioritisation, a structured HPI/summary artifact, provider edit-before-chart, and outcome-based ROI framing (time saved, patient ease, throughput). (3) It also exposes exactly where MediKiosk differentiates: DAINA is cloud-only, US-resident, English/Spanish-first, writes into proprietary EHR fields via HL7v2, and is not tied to any open national summary contract - so it supplies no path to NRCeS OPConsultRecord, offline operation, India data residency, or an AYUSH-aware bilingual summary. It is a validation benchmark, not a substitute.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (a) protocol-driven, specialty-configurable elicitation as the summary engine's upstream - the summary quality is bounded by the protocol, so Module C should consume a similarly structured, protocol-shaped history bundle; (b) red-flag-first questioning and explicit red-flag surfacing with triage categories (already aligned with MediKiosk's urgent-flag banner); (c) the provider-edits-before-chart workflow, which maps cleanly onto MediKiosk's physician attestation and is the human-oversight control that keeps an elicit-never-diagnose agent safe; (d) outcome-based evaluation framing (time-saved/visit, patient ease, throughput) as a pilot metric set, paired with the independent methodology MediKiosk already plans; (e) multi-channel input (phone and in-person kiosk/tablet) since MediKiosk's kiosk can serve both; (f) reading organisation guidelines into structured protocols and keeping them as reviewable, versionable artifacts. Adapt: the summary should be generated deterministically against a fixed output contract, not as free text. Reject: (a) cloud-only, US-resident inference (Module C must run offline on a ~4GB CPU/iGPU kiosk); (b) proprietary, opaque models and undisclosed ASR/TTS (Module C needs auditable, license-clear components); (c) HL7v2-write-into-proprietary-EHR as the terminal artifact (MediKiosk must emit a portable, validated NRCeS FHIR document); (d) the absence of published accuracy/omission metrics - MediKiosk should not ship a pre-visit summariser without its own eval harness.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: Key risks and gaps: (1) No published clinical-accuracy, omission or hallucination metrics - the central safety question for a note-writing intake agent is unanswered, and third parties explicitly flag this. (2) Evidence is company-reported (pilot survey via LinkedIn, marketing claims), not independently audited or peer-reviewed; the '8 min', '93%', '$3,600/month' and '300+ patients' figures all originate from the vendor. (3) The seed amount itself is inconsistent in the public record - $2.8M in the 5 August 2026 AZBio/company announcement and Phoenix Business Journal, but 'undisclosed' in the later 26 August 2026 Business Wire version, a genuine disclosure discrepancy. (4) Single-specialty evidence (cardiology/arrhythmia) - scalability across specialties, languages, populations and EHR configurations is unproven, as the vendor's own use-of-funds notes (broadening protocols, deepening safety checks, more EHR integrations). (5) Multilingual breadth is claimed but the language list, accent/dialect robustness and quality evidence are unpublished, and a pre-visit voice agent is highly exposed to accent/dialect and elderly/hearing-impaired failure modes. (6) Cloud-only with US/Azure-Gov residency, no offline path - disqualifying for MediKiosk's constraints. (7) No document-digitisation pipeline and no AYUSH/Indic terminology - it cannot consume the paper documents Module B digitises. (8) Heavy market competition from better-capitalised adjacent players (Assort Health $120M Series C at $1.2B with intake/triage scope; Hippocratic AI $444M with a large safety-validation programme; Hyro; Luma; Phreesia; Interactly) means the generic 'AI intake' story is quickly commoditised, so MediKiosk cannot rely on intake novelty alone.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: Overlap: both are patient-facing, pre-visit, conversational history-elicitation systems that turn a dialogue into a structured note for a clinician, both prioritise red flags, and both are designed to be reviewed/edited by the provider rather than to diagnose. Difference is nearly total on the four MediKiosk differentiators: (1) Offline - DAINA is cloud-only in a dedicated US Azure tenant; MediKiosk must run offline on a ~4GB CPU/iGPU kiosk. (2) India data residency - DAINA offers US regions only; MediKiosk must keep data in India. (3) NRCeS-conformant emission - DAINA writes EHR-native intake notes via HL7v2, with no FHIR/national-IG document; MediKiosk emits a physician-attested NRCeS OPConsultRecord/document Bundle for ABDM (and now, per NRCeS v7.0.0 preview, potentially the INPS patient-summary profile). (4) Bilingual/AYUSH history with per-field provenance - DAINA is English/Spanish-centric with no Devanagari/Hinglish or AYUSH terminology and no published provenance model; MediKiosk targets Hindi/English and AYUSH clinical frameworks with per-field provenance. Net effect: DAINA strongly STRENGTHENS MediKiosk's thesis (it de-risks the core 'will a pre-visit elicited note help the clinician?' question and sets the ROI/breadth bar) while leaving every one of MediKiosk's structural differentiators untouched. The main erosion risk is reputational, not technical: judges may see 'an AI intake agent' as already-done, so MediKiosk must lead with offline + India-resident + NRCeS-conformant + transparent-provenance rather than the intake conversation itself.

business_info.license: Proprietary, closed-source commercial software. No open-source license; models and ASR/TTS components are not disclosed.
business_info.pricing: Not published. Sold via 'Book a demo' / 'Get in touch' (hello@miihealth.ai); a public ROI calculator frames value as 8 minutes saved per visit across 16 patients/provider/day at a $90/hour provider rate (~$3,600 saved monthly per provider in the company's own example). No self-serve tier or free trial is advertised. [uncertain - no list price]
business_info.funding: $2.8M seed round announced 5 August 2026 (AZBio/company release) led by Russell Glass, former CEO of Headspace and founder/General Partner of Arteria Capital, with participation from unnamed physician angels, healthcare operators and digital-health founders. The later Business Wire release (26 August 2026) describes the amount as 'undisclosed', so the capital figure carries a public disclosure discrepancy. No valuation or terms disclosed. The company is a 2024 Mayo Clinic & ASU MedTech Accelerator alum (via predecessor MiiCare) and relocated from London to Phoenix in 2024.
business_info.commercial_status: Venture-backed commercial company (seed stage) selling to US health systems, specialty practices and virtual-first providers; still largely pilot/validation stage rather than broad production. Non-US, non-commercial, or open implementations: none.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: Adjacent and direct: conversational pre-visit intake - Perspective AI, Interactly, Assort Health (intake/triage/referrals; $120M Series C June 2026 at $1.2B), Hippocratic AI (clinical-adjacent outreach, $444M raised, 1,000+ guardrailed agents), Hello Patient, Simbie AI, DeepCura; AI phone/reception - Hyro, Luma Health (ARIA), Klara, Emitrr, Retell AI, Bland AI; administrative intake/check-in kiosks - Phreesia, Doctible; ambient scribes that increasingly add pre-visit chart summaries - Abridge, Ambience Healthcare, Microsoft Dragon Copilot, Suki, Nabla, Sunoh.ai; Indian comparators - Eka Care (ABDM PHR + EkaScribe). DAINA's distinct wedge is 'autonomous outbound pre-visit clinical intake with EHR writeback', which few rivals combine.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: Major US EHRs via HL7v2 and 'other standards' (specific EHRs not named); phone/telephony integrations; web/mobile/tablet channels; dedicated Microsoft Azure single-tenant hosting. No ABDM gateway role (HIP/HIU/PHR), no ABHA/Health Locker integration, no Indian HIS/EHR integrations, no FHIR API described.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: The AI-patient-voice/intake category is consolidating and well-capitalised in the US (Assort Health, Hippocratic AI, Hyro, Luma, Interactly), with 'governed actions inside the EHR' becoming table stakes and several vendors explicitly pushing clinician-reviewed, safety-guardrailed agents. This creates a US category MediKiosk does not compete in directly. For MediKiosk the relevant ecosystem fact is that none of these players is building for India's ABDM/NRCeS output contract, offline kiosk operation, India data residency, or AYUSH terminology - the structural niche remains open. Conversely, DAINA's Mayo Clinic credibility may make 'pre-visit AI intake' a familiar, accepted category by the time MediKiosk is judged, which is a net tailwind if MediKiosk leads with its ABDM/offline/AYUSH differentiators.

market_positioning.target_users: US health systems, specialty practices, medical groups and virtual-first providers; explicitly positioned for older adults and for clinicians/front-desk staff who want the pre-visit chart prepared before the encounter. Patients are the conversational end-users; providers are the primary buyer value.
market_positioning.market_segment: Pre-visit patient intake / agentic clinical intake automation - the 'front door of care'. It sits adjacent to, and markets itself against, ambient clinical documentation/scribing, and adjacent to AI phone/receptionist and check-in platforms.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: Pitches itself as 'the first agentic AI medical assistant purpose-built to automate patient intake' and Mediiflow as 'the world's first clinic-ready AI intake engine' that is 'built for healthcare's highest standards' - promising an autonomous, multilingual, empathetic pre-visit conversation that captures structured history and red flags and hands providers an EHR-ready note, returning 'more than two hours a day' and enabling 'more care, less admin'. Its trust pitch is a dedicated, isolated, single-tenant Microsoft Azure environment ('every hospital should be a data fortress').
